Tim / Ruth / Hannah —

Quick sketch of scenarios based on the CSV: I ran three clean scenarios (numbers are illustrative; final will come after we confirm concurrency SLA targets):

Scenario A — Hosted PAYG
- Unit basis: per-1M tokens generation + inference overhead (no commit)
- Estimated cost: $1,200 per 1M tokens (weighted by mix above)
- Pros: zero commit, flexible; Cons: higher tail cost during peak retrain windows

Scenario B — Short pilot (3 months) + Pilot credits
- Offer: 20% pilot credit applied during 3-month pilot up to $30k, plus 10% committed capacity discount if move to reserved within 45 days
- Estimated effective cost during pilot: $960 per 1M tokens (after credits)
- Operational suggestion: reserve a small dedicated pool sized for 30% of peak concurrency to cover low-latency paths; route the rest to hosted.

Scenario C — 12-month reserved capacity
- Offer: tiered reserved pricing; base discount 35% vs PAYG for a 12-mo commit sized to 70% of forecasted run-rate, additional 5–10% for upfront prepay
- Estimated cost: $780 per 1M tokens (base), $700 per 1M tokens (with 10% prepay)

Technical levers and packaging notes:
- Quantized model variants for long-generation endpoints reduce GPU time ~18–25% (applies to the 5% long-gen bucket).
- Autoscaling policy: capped burst to hosted reduces reserve sizing and can lower overall commit by ~12% with modest latency tradeoff.
- Onboarding credit: if Polaris signs reserved within 60 days, we extend one-time migration credit equal to 10% of first-quarter run-rate.

Related links: hubspot pipeline (https://hubspot.company/r/PL-2026-381) and shared pilot folder (https://drive.company/shared/polaris-pilot-pack) where I dropped a sample term sheet and the cost model.

If this looks reasonable, Hannah — can you draft a clean pilot term sheet (30–45 day convert window) and include the pilot credit and recommended reserve sizing? Tim / Ruth — any immediate redlines from procurement we should anticipate?

—Karthik
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
